'''Erenhiko Shrine''' (えれひこじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Nagahama, Shiga|Q844130|qid=Q844130}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
{{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|lt=Ōyamakui-no-Kami|Q10935105|qid=Q10935105}} is the principal deity, with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Hiboko-no-Mikoto}} enshrined as an associated deity.

=== Shrine crest ===
Konoe peony

=== History ===
It is said that during the time of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, descendants of Ame-no-Hiboko-no-Mikoto developed this area and enshrined their ancestral deity. Later, when the land became territory of {{ill|Enryaku-ji|Q917195|qid=Q917195}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hiyoshi Sannō Gongen}} (Ōyamakui-no-Kami), who was the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=guardian deity}} of the temple, was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=invited and enshrined}}, and the deities were {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}. In the first year of {{ill|Genryaku|Q1194250|qid=Q1194250}} ({{ill|1184|Q19728|qid=Q19728}}), land within the precincts was donated, but the shrine buildings fell into ruin during the {{ill|Battle of Shizugatake|Q225562|qid=Q225562}}. In the 7th year of {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} ({{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}}), land was again donated as tax-exempt land and the shrine was restored. In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 55 ({{ill|1980|Q2439|qid=Q2439}}), because the {{ill|Hokuriku Expressway|Q1549512|qid=Q1549512}} came to pass through the precincts, new shrine buildings and other structures were constructed. This shrine is the small shrine “Namarenihiko Shrine” of Ōmi Province listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} (a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}). In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 9 ({{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Rituals ===
